complexity_scope.guarantee: Complexity: per-instance success >=2/3 with per-instance almost-sure cap; deterministic guaranteed success. Fixed-distribution strengthening: every all-history capped randomized policy has average success <=1/3.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: c_p,C_p,epsilon_p may depend on p; polynomial dimension is sufficient, not optimal.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact joint value-gradient oracle only, arbitrary finite Euclidean queries.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Arbitrary measurable x_out in R^d, possibly unqueried; ||gradient f(x_out)||<=epsilon.
complexity_scope.regime: Normalized gap and directional budgets all <=1; epsilon sufficiently small depending on fixed finite p.
complexity_scope.resource: Number of joint oracle calls; supremum over all finite dimensions, not expected calls or practical runtime.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper: deterministic Carmon et al. [2] exact first-order method imported through Appendix F's quadratic lift. Lower: every unrestricted measurable adaptive randomized policy; no span or zero-respecting restriction.

map: Import analytic interfaces from A.2–A.5 pp.10–14, read as source-linked literature arguments: H=gamma I+L P_M, a=A 1_suffix/sqrt(|suffix|), e=e_1; alpha=a^T H^(-1)e, beta=a^T H^(-1)a, rho=e^T H^(-1)e, lambda=1/alpha, tau=1/beta, kappa=rho/alpha^2. F=sum_s[z_s^T H z_s/2-lambda u_{s-1}e^T z_s+kappa u_s^2/2+tau phi_r(u_s)], u_s=a^T z_s,u_0=1. A.2 scalar transition and A.3 exact terminal residual identity yield the zero-tail gradient certificate; do not delete its terminal boundary term.

A.5: for small b>0, G_0=8192,L=b/16, C_*=max_{1<=q<=p}C_q, choose a_0 with 18G_0 C_* a_0^3<=b/4. Set A=r=a_0 epsilon^(-1/3), gamma=G_0 a_0 epsilon^(2/3), h=sqrt(gamma/L), M=ceil(1/h), N=floor(a_0 epsilon^(-4/3)/(1440G_0)). Then derivatives orders 2,...,p+1 have full operator norm <=b, gap <=1/4, and u_N=0 forces ||gradient F||>=32epsilon. Cancellation tau A^(q+1)r^(3-q)=tau A^4 preserves the exponent.

A.3 and B.1–B.3 pp.12–18: use K extra PSD quadratic copies and one Haar rotation. Add P_Z(y)=sigma_3 Z_3[y,y,y]/3+sigma_4 Z_4[y,y,y,y]/4, independent static isonormal tensors with sigma_k=delta_k/(a_k sqrt(d)), a_k=4sqrt(k log(1+4k)+2). For R=epsilon^(-1), eta_0=4epsilon^2, delta_3=epsilon^3/8,delta_4=epsilon^4/8, form f=(F_U+P_Z)(rho_R(x))+eta_0||x||^2/2, rho_R(x)=x/sqrt(1+||x||^2/R^2). Norm event G_Z has probability >=1-4exp(-4d). For b<=1/(16pK_*) and sufficiently small epsilon, B.2 gives global derivative budgets <=1 and gap <=1/3 on G_Z.

Robust B.2 interface: |b_N^T rho_R(x)|<=16epsilon/b implies ||gradient f(x)||>epsilon. For ||x||>=R the radial lower bound alone exceeds 3epsilon. Inside R, subtracting the terminal-readout component changes the base gradient by at most b|a_N^T y|/A; the zero-tail certificate leaves >=16epsilon, mask gradient <=epsilon/4, Jacobian minimum singular value >=1/(2sqrt2), and radial quadratic costs <=4epsilon. Thus (16epsilon-epsilon/4)/(2sqrt2)-4epsilon>epsilon.

C–D pp.18–30: scheduled repeated-spectrum Haar control applies to the reference process after fixing independent physical innovation seeds. Theorem D.2 factors the exact two-channel posterior and charges KL only to Delta V. Corollary D.6 telescopes observation increments; Proposition D.7 couples complete histories with the same static U,Z,seed until first hidden-core exit. Tensor norm conditioning occurs only after the unconditioned KL calculation.

E.2 pp.31–34: j_*=ceil(M/2), T=floor(Nj_*/2), L_cand=T+1, K=ceil(epsilon^(-14)), zeta=K^(-4), d=(K+1)NM. Layer (s-1)j_*+min(j,j_*) ensures Qbar I_t subset I_{t+1}, readout disclosure tau_s=s j_*. Final candidate is frozen and receives no response. With w_3=-120tau A^3=O_p(epsilon^(1/3)),w_4=120tau A^4=O_p(1), KL<=C_p[epsilon^(-13)/K+epsilon^(-52/3)/K^2+epsilon^(-37/3)/K^3]=O_p(epsilon). Whole-span theta^2=O_p(epsilon^(37/3)), so Rtheta=O_p(epsilon^(31/6)) meets both core and terminal thresholds.

Pinsker plus first-exit coupling bounds success under conditioned static D_{p,epsilon} by [zeta+sqrt(KL/2)]/[1-4exp(-4d)]=O_p(sqrt(epsilon))<=1/3. The distribution is fixed independently of policy; only the auxiliary geometric coupling/event may depend on policy. E.2.5 truncates per-instance almost-sure capped policies on all histories, integrates null seed sets, then averages to contradict per-instance success >=2/3. T=Theta_p(epsilon^(-5/3)) and d=O_p(epsilon^(-47/3)).

proofs.full_local_argument: Imported interface from Appendix F's quotation of Carmon et al. [2], not independently verified here: for directional L1=L3=1, actual gap Delta and epsilon^(2/3)<=min(sqrt(Delta),1/8), a deterministic method uses O(Delta epsilon^(-5/3)log(500Delta/epsilon^2)) value/gradient evaluations with the same asymptotic bundle cost, without needing inf f as input. For f in H_{p,d}, define tilde f(x,t)=f(x)+(t-1)^2/2 and start (0,0). Its gap is Delta_f+1/2 in [1/2,3/2]. The block-diagonal gradient is 1-Lipschitz. In a unit line direction (v,a), the quadratic contributes no third derivative; the Lipschitz variation of the original third directional derivative scales by ||v||^4<=1. Hence L1=L3=1 remains valid. For epsilon^(2/3)<=1/8 the imported accuracy condition holds uniformly. One query (x,t) needs exactly one original (f(x),gradient f(x)); add the known quadratic value and gradient. Since ||gradient tilde f||^2=||gradient f(x)||^2+(t-1)^2, dropping t preserves epsilon-stationarity. Delta<=3/2 makes the cost O(epsilon^(-5/3)log(2/epsilon)). Deterministic success also supplies the randomized upper bound. This proves only the local lifting/simulation conditional on the stated imported upper-bound interface.

assumptions: p is finite and fixed independently of epsilon; constants may depend on p.
Every query is any finite point of R^d and returns exactly (f(x),gradient f(x)), with no higher derivatives. Query norms and computation between calls are unrestricted.
Policies and outputs are measurable, all seed/advice/transcript spaces standard Borel; output need not have been queried.
Each objective is fixed independently of the algorithm's private seed. The complexity definition uses per-fixed-instance almost-sure query caps, not expected costs.
statement.conclusion: c_p epsilon^(-5/3)<=Q_p^(infinity,rand)(epsilon)<=Q_p^(infinity,det)(epsilon)<=C_p epsilon^(-5/3)log(2/epsilon), together with the single-distribution dimension and failure guarantee above.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For d>=1 and fixed integer p>=3, H_{p,d}={f in C-infinity(R^d):f(0)-inf f<=1; for f_{x,v}(t)=f(x+tv), |f_{x,v}^(q)(t)-f_{x,v}^(q)(s)|<=|t-s| for every q=1,...,p, x in R^d, unit v and s,t in R}. Norms of vectors are Euclidean. Q_p^rand(d,epsilon) is the least integer T for which one algorithm makes <=T exact value-gradient calls almost surely on each fixed admissible f and returns ||gradient f(x_out)||<=epsilon with probability >=2/3 for every such f. Deterministic Q requires guaranteed success. Q_p^(infinity,rand/det)=sup_{d>=1}Q_p^(rand/det)(d,epsilon).
statement.parameter_domains: d positive integer; fixed finite integer p>=3; 0<epsilon<=epsilon_p. Hard dimension may grow as accuracy improves; no fixed-d lower bound or uniform-in-p limit.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed finite p>=3 there exist c_p,C_p,epsilon_p>0 such that for every 0<epsilon<=epsilon_p the inequalities hold. More precisely there exist an integer d_epsilon<=C_p epsilon^(-47/3) and one distribution D_{p,epsilon} supported on H_{p,d_epsilon}, independent of the policy and private seed, such that every measurable randomized policy with all-history pathwise cap floor(c_p epsilon^(-5/3)) has average success <=1/3 over D_{p,epsilon} and its independent seed. Per-instance almost-sure caps reduce to this convention by all-history truncation without changing behavior except on each fixed function's null seed set.
